Today, President Donald J. Trump returns to the Magnolia State to highlight a proven record of results that put Mississippi workers, families, seniors, farmers, and communities first. Under the leadership of President Trump and Republicans, Mississippians are benefiting from historic tax relief, surging private investment and job creation, stronger rural healthcare, major support for farmers, and new resources for the state’s defense and shipbuilding industry.

Delivering Tax Relief for Hardworking Mississippians

President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts are putting real money back in the pockets of Mississippi workers, families, and seniors.

  • No Tax on Social Security: Approximately 500,000 Mississippi seniors benefit from the new senior deduction, with the average senior expected to pay zero federal taxes on Social Security benefits.
  • Bigger Refunds: Mississippi taxpayers saw average refunds of $4,018 in 2026 — among the highest in the nation.
  • Protecting Jobs and Wages: The Working Families Tax Cuts safeguarded 46,000 Mississippi jobs, $8 billion in state GDP, and $4 billion in workers’ wages.
  • Lowering Taxes for Family Farms and Small Businesses: The tax cuts made the increased death tax exemption permanent and indexed it for inflation, made 100% expensing permanent, doubled the Section 179 limit, made the 20% small business deduction permanent, expanded crop insurance, and increased reference prices for the first time in over a decade.
  • Strengthening the Farm Safety Net: The Working Families Tax Cuts delivered more than $469 million in farm safety net and conservation program payments to Mississippi farmers, producers, and landowners — part of the first meaningful investment in these programs in decades.

Strengthening Rural Healthcare Across Mississippi

President Trump is delivering targeted resources to expand access, modernize care, and improve outcomes in Mississippi’s rural communities.

  • Rural Health Transformation: Mississippi secured $206 million in first-year funding from the Working Families Tax Cuts’ Rural Health Transformation Program — one of the largest awards among all states — to expand access, strengthen the workforce, and streamline care.
  • Modernizing Care Delivery: The Trump Administration awarded more than $104 million through 167 grants for Mississippi rural health technology upgrades, specialty and maternal care, and telehealth.
  • Advancing Telehealth: The Trump Administration awarded the University of Mississippi Medical Center $4.25 million to renew its status as a federal Center of Excellence in Telehealth — one of only two in the country — expanding remote care for rural and underserved communities.

Unleashing Private Investment and Job Creation

President Trump’s pro-growth, America First agenda is driving major private investment and job creation throughout the Magnolia State, from advanced manufacturing to logistics, shipbuilding, and technology.

  • ALO is investing $176 million to open a national distribution center in Southaven, creating more than 400 jobs.
  • Gulf Ship is investing $44 million to modernize its Gulfport shipyard, creating 121 jobs.
  • Raytheon is investing $50 million to expand its electronic warfare and radar systems manufacturing facility in Forest, creating 100 jobs.
  • Southwire is investing $256 million to expand its Starkville operations, creating 128 jobs.
  • Aluminum Dynamics is investing $200 million to develop a recycled aluminum slab center in Lowndes County, creating 100 jobs.
  • SIP Manufacturing is investing more than $100 million to build a production, packaging, and shipping facility in Southaven, creating 187 jobs.
  • Amazon is investing an additional $12 billion in part to expand the company’s data center operation in Madison County, creating 700 jobs, in addition to a $3 billion project in Vicksburg announced last year.
  • Southwark Metal Manufacturing Company is investing $29 million to expand its operations in DeSoto County.
  • Siemens Energy is investing $300 million to build a new manufacturing facility for electrical grid components in Pearl, creating up to 300 jobs.
  • xAI is investing $20 billion to build a data center in Southaven, creating hundreds of jobs.
  • BWC Terminals is investing $316 million to locate a terminal facility in Pascagoula.
  • Hood Industries is investing $245 million to construct a new advanced sawmill in Waynesboro.

Rebuilding Communities and Upgrading Infrastructure

President Trump is delivering federal resources to help Mississippi recover from storms, reduce congestion, and strengthen freight movement that supports economic growth.

  • Helping Mississippi Rebuild: In August 2026, President Trump approved Mississippi’s disaster declaration request for counties impacted by Tropical Storm Arthur, unlocking individual and public assistance. Earlier federal disaster assistance was approved following May 2026 severe storms, including funds for temporary housing and home repairs, low-cost loans for uninsured losses, and other recovery programs.
  • Expanding Critical Corridors: In October 2026, the Trump Administration awarded a $44 million grant to expand the I-55/I-69 corridor in DeSoto County from four to ten lanes, add ramp and turning lanes, and lengthen acceleration and deceleration lanes — reducing congestion on a vital freight route that serves tens of thousands of vehicles daily.
  • Upgrading Mississippi Roads: In July 2026, the Trump Administration awarded $51.1 million in federal BUILD grants to improve U.S. Highway 80 in Brandon, expand truck parking along I-10 in Hancock County, and upgrade Mallett Road in D’Iberville.
  • Modernizing Freight Rail: The Trump Administration awarded Mississippi Export Railroad up to $35.5 million to modernize and automate a 121-year-old swing bridge, upgrade track, improve crossings, and raise track in flood-prone areas — strengthening reliability for Gulf Coast industries and ports.

Putting Mississippi Farmers First

President Trump is delivering direct support, infrastructure upgrades, and market opportunities for Mississippi agriculture.

  • Emergency Assistance: The Trump Administration has delivered more than $145 million to nearly 4,300 Mississippi farmers and producers through the Emergency Commodity Assistance Program. Nearly 3,700 Mississippi producers have also received more than $147 million in payments as part of a $12 billion national bridge program for trade disruptions and higher input costs left by the Biden Administration. Hundreds of Mississippi producers have also received more than $8 million in funding through the Assistance for Specialty Crop Farmers program.
  • Support for Ranchers: In September 2026, President Trump signed two Executive Orders to back American ranchers — one directing action to help producers protect herds from wolves and other predators and advancing country-of-origin labeling transparency, and another strengthening enforcement of the Packers and Stockyards Act to expand market access without compromising food safety.

Investing in Mississippi’s Military and Defense Industries

President Trump is delivering new resources to strengthen Mississippi’s shipbuilding and defense capabilities, supporting both national security and high-quality jobs.

  • In October 2026, the Navy awarded a $99 million contract to Ingalls Shipbuilding in Pascagoula for sea trials of the USS Lyndon B. Johnson.
  • In April 2026, the Navy awarded a $283 million contract to begin work on the Navy’s new FF(X) frigate combatant ships.
  • In February 2026, Mississippi secured $528 million in NDAA funding, including $53 million for critical upgrades at Columbus Air Force Base, Camp Shelby, Navy Reserve Center Meridian, and Key Field Air National Guard Base.

President Trump and Republicans are delivering lower taxes, major private investment, stronger support for farmers and rural communities, and new resources for Mississippi’s military. Mississippians face a clear choice: continue this progress, or return to the higher taxes, open borders, and failed policies of the past.
